Issue_Reported: At the end of Reconditioning, it was noticed by the test operator, B. Crowell, the subject appeared to have a broken capillary in the right eye. The subject did know it was there and did not express any pain or discomfort. It is not known if the broken capillary was there before the reconditioning session. The reconditioning session involved stretching and walking. It was noted on the CRF the broken capillary could have happened during a stretching session where the subject holds their head below the waist for 30 seconds.
Description_of_Action_Taken: The Study Lead has spoken with the test operator. The test operator has some suggestions on how to work around the broken capillary for future Reconditioning sessions but has some concerns for Project Science as well.
Disposition_Comments: The broken capillary may have indeed occurred during stretching as the subject bends over to touch toes for 30 seconds. Attending physician, David Ware, saw the subject and confirmed the scleral hemorrhage with no pain or visual loss. Stretching protocols for this subject were modified to avoid the forward bending position. The subject was reported to be doing well with no resultant discomfort. All required paperwork was filed including UTMB IRB Adverse Event and Unanticipated Problem Report Form.

Issue_Reported: The subject experienced a significant drop in blood pressure and heart rate during Tilt test. Test resulted in blood pressure of ~96/48 and a heart rate of 65.
Description_of_Action_Taken: Vital signs were assessed by nurse and determined that additional medical evaluation was required before test administration of sublingual nitroglycerin. Coordinator on Duty (COD) was notified and COD notified Study Lead and back up with continued updates. Notification of Project Science provided by Study Lead. The subject was monitored closely after the test and in just over an hour the subject's blood pressure and heart rate were within normal limits. Subject met the attending physician's criteria to proceed but on a delayed timeline. The test eventually proceeded with the Medical Monitor present in the room. The end result was a delay of 1.75 hours in the Sublingual Nitroglycerin portion of Vascular Function test.
Disposition_Comments: Changes in blood pressure and heart rate are expected during the Tilt test. These symptoms, when observed after the completion of the Tilt test, are likely to be related to the Tilt testing. This was reported as an Adverse Event but an Anticipated Event. The subject was seen by Principal Investigator (PI) David Ware, MD. No medical treatment was required. The subject was reported as doing well and not expected to have any long-term problems. All pertinent paperwork was filed including the UTMB IRB Adverse Event and Unanticipated Problem Report Form.

Issue_Reported: Attending physician David Ware, MD ordered an unscheduled 4 mL blood draw for complete blood count.
Description_of_Action_Taken: A total of 4 mL of blood was drawn and taken to the lab. Coordinator on Duty (COD) notified.
Disposition_Comments: The Complete Blood Count was ordered from the UTMB lab to confirm the prior NASA Clinical lab's results. The NASA Clinical Laboratory had reported a drop in this subject's hemoglobin and hematocrit values between blood draws taken on May 29th and June 3rd. Dr. Ware believes this is the result of hemodilution, since the subject has been drinking 6 liters of water each day for the past 6 days. Since the diuretic effect of head down tilt no longer exists, there is less hemoconcentration. Results of the repeat testing show the subject results returning to normal. The additional draw did not cause exceedance of the blood draw limits. All applicable paperwork was filed including the IRB Protocol Deviation Report.
